reply_text:
I found one dated AI prediction by Sam Altman from 2017, and I read it in a transcript published by a third party rather than on Altman's or Google's own page. In a Talks at Google interview from about mid-August 2017, he said AI "has the potential to eliminate nearly all human suffering in the next couple of decades." I dated it to August 2017 from what he said in the talk, not from a printed date. He referred to OpenAI beating the best single Dota players "last Friday", which points to the week after 11 August 2017. He also said "we get to vote again in 3 and 1/2 more years", which fits mid-2017. Note that he says "has the potential", so this is a hedged forecast.

- **The Merge (blog, 7 December 2017):** He writes that the merge of humans and machines is "probably going to happen sooner than most people think." He gives no date of his own. The 2025–2075 range in the essay is what he says *other people* guess, so it should not be credited to him as a prediction. I read the essay as a reprint on churchandstate.org.uk, which says it was reprinted with the author's permission. I could not open his own blog page because the fetch tool refused it.
- **Other years:** A StrictlyVC podcast summary has him saying a smarter-than-human software system will be built "in the next few decades". The page dates from about 2019, so it is not a 2017 statement. The "2017 Greylock interview" in a Substack essay could not be checked. Greylock's own pages show Altman interviews only from 2022 onward, so I did not use it.
- **Pages that would not open:** Altman's own pages for The Merge and The United Slate, and Wikiquote. The United Slate is his July 2017 political platform, and coverage says it touches on AI. I didn't read it, so it may contain a dated claim.

I used 9 of 12 searches and all 6 page openings, counting the four failed ones. I left the other 3 searches unused because I had no openings left to check anything they found.
